permit_authority.value: City of South Portland Code Enforcement (Department of Planning and Development)
permit_authority.notes: Maine's Uniform Building and Energy Code (MUBEC) is mandatory statewide for municipalities with more than 4,000 residents (smaller towns may opt out of enforcement but cannot substitute a different building code) — a genuinely uniform statewide baseline, though enforcement is local. South Portland's own Code Enforcement division is the local AHJ. State law requires municipalities to exclusively employ code enforcement officers certified by Maine's Department of Economic and Community Development.

interconnection_url.notes: CMP's own Net Energy Billing page did not load successfully this session (repeated timeout). Maine's net metering program is branded 'Net Energy Billing' and is administered under Maine PUC rules (Chapter 313 for net energy billing, Chapter 324 for the Interconnection Agreement); customers must file both applications with CMP before service begins. This structural detail is recorded with moderate confidence, pending direct confirmation of CMP's own page content.

value.name: Solar Energy Equipment Property Tax Exemption
value.administrator: Maine Revenue Services / municipal assessors, per 36 M.R.S. §§ 655(1)(U)-(V), 656(1)(K)-(L)
value.description: Statewide property tax exemption for solar equipment that generates heat or electricity, for assessments made on or after 2025-04-01. A residential array qualifies if all energy generated is used on site, or the equipment is collocated with a net-energy-billing customer subscribed to at least 50% of the facility's output, or the energy is transmitted through facilities with a utility bill credit. Eligible equipment includes solar panels, racking/tracking hardware, inverters, batteries used to store panel-generated electricity, charge controllers, and related wiring — meters and grid-side equipment are not eligible. Equipment under construction and not yet operational on April 1 does not qualify for that tax year. The exemption must be claimed by filing a report with the local assessor.
value.eligibility: Residential solar array in Maine meeting the on-site-use or net-energy-billing collocation/transmission conditions above; a report must be filed with the municipal assessor on or before April 1 of the first tax year claimed.

rebates.notes: Statewide fact per Maine Revenue Services' own Property Tax Bulletin No. 29 (December 2024), reused here per the multi-state/statewide reuse convention — this is a state law provision, not a South-Portland-specific program. This is a property-tax exemption, not a cash rebate; multiple third-party solar-industry sites this session independently converged on 'no state solar cash rebate exists in Maine, only this property tax exemption plus net metering,' consistent with what was found in the primary source.
